body.statement:
For fixed \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), put
\[
 M_A=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4,
 \qquad
 M_B=M_A\,k(k-1)(2k-1)^4,
 \qquad
 M_{k,\ell}=M_A+M_B.                                      \tag{29}
\]
The design-A and design-B structural enumerations used by \(\mathscr A\) have at most \(M_A\) and \(M_B\) charts, respectively.  Every chart has a semialgebraic description with at most
\[
 N_0=4\ell+10k+12,
 \qquad
 S_0=100(k\ell+k^2+\ell+1),
 \qquad
 D_0=4                                                     \tag{30}
\]
variables, polynomial sign atoms, and polynomial degree.

Let \(\mathsf{Samp}\), \(\mathsf{Exist}\), and \(\mathsf{Enc}\) be coordinatewise nondecreasing versions of the explicit published output-format bounds for, respectively, semialgebraic emptiness with one real-univariate sample, existential realizability with one sample over an ordered algebraic coefficient extension, and primitive-element, square-free, Thom-sign, comparison, and rational-isolation normalization.  In \(\mathsf{Exist}(N,S,D;\delta)\), the last input bounds the coefficient-extension degree, and the returned degree is absolute over the original input field.  Define
\[
 (A_S,D_S)=\mathsf{Samp}(N_0,S_0,D_0),                    \tag{31}
\]
\[
 (A_E,D_E)=\mathsf{Exist}(N_0,S_0+1,D_0;D_S),
 \qquad
 (A_R,D_R)=\mathsf{Enc}(D_S,D_E),                          \tag{32}
\]
and
\[
 B_{k,\ell}=M_{k,\ell}
 (2+A_S)(2+A_E)(2+A_R)
 (1+D_S)(1+D_E)(1+D_R).                                   \tag{33}
\]
Then \(B_{k,\ell}\) is explicit and computable and bounds both the total number of labeled intermediate and final records and every absolute real-univariate algebraic degree produced by the compiler.

Let \(Q=k\ell+k^2+\ell+1\) and \(\operatorname{Exp}_2(x)=2^x\).  The singly-exponential critical-point sampling, existential-realizability, and real-univariate encoding bounds imply that, for a universal constant \(C\ge1\),
\[
 B_{k,\ell}\le \operatorname{Exp}_2(CQ^C).                \tag{34}
\]
Over an arbitrary real input field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), the computation terminates relative to effective field arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles.

For rational input coordinates of numerator and denominator binary length at most \(L\), let \(\mathsf{Samp}_h\), \(\mathsf{Exist}_h\), and \(\mathsf{Enc}_h\) be the corresponding published integer-coefficient height bounds and define sequentially
\[
 h_0=64Q^2(L+1),
 \qquad
 h_S=\mathsf{Samp}_h(N_0,S_0,D_0,h_0),                    \tag{35}
\]
\[
 h_E=\mathsf{Exist}_h(N_0,S_0+1,D_0;D_S,h_S),
 \qquad
 H_{k,\ell}(L)=\mathsf{Enc}_h(D_S,D_E,h_S,h_E).            \tag{36}
\]
After guarded denominators are cleared, every algebraic target or witness certificate has a square-free integer real-univariate representation of degree at most \(B_{k,\ell}\), with coefficient and rational-isolating-endpoint binary lengths at most \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\).  A Turing implementation terminates, and after increasing the universal constant in (34) if necessary,
\[
 H_{k,\ell}(L)
 \le \operatorname{Exp}_2(CQ^C)
 (L+1)^{\operatorname{Exp}_2(CQ^C)}.                       \tag{37}
\]
The decision first enumerates and tests the structural charts, samples one feasible \(x_0\), and then performs one existential disagreement test per chart over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(\tau_C(x_0))\).  Connected-component descriptions and target projections are optional diagnostics and are not part of the decision or of bounds (31)--(37); no generic two-copy unequal-target formula is used.
body.justification: The theorem bounds the executed sequence of chart enumeration, one feasible sample, chartwise existential disagreement, and exact encoding.
body.gap: The former bounds charged for connected-component and projection stages that are no longer part of the decision.
body.consumer: Implementations obtain an honest fixed-alphabet singly-exponential degree and rational-height contract with ordered coefficient extensions made explicit.
body.proof_tex:
We verify the chart and format bounds in the order used by the revised compiler.

A vector \(b_i\in\Delta_{\mathcal W}\) has a nonempty support and hence at most \(2^{\ell}-1\) labeled support patterns.  The four response vertices contribute at most
\[
 (2^{\ell}-1)^4.                                           \tag{38}
\]
By selected-table positivity, \(v_e(z)>0\).  In a rank-two cell, the two orientations and the three coefficient-support states at each \(z\) give at most \(2\cdot3^k\) modes.  By \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\), rank one contributes \(3^k\) coordinatewise faces in mode \(\mathrm E\) and the three further modes \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm D\).  Thus one cell contributes at most
\[
 2\cdot3^k+3^k+3=3^{k+1}+3.                               \tag{39}
\]
There are four cells, so (38) times the fourth power of (39) proves the formula for \(M_A\).

For design B, each of the four response links has one zero-residual state or an active state recording one of \(k-1\) first nonbaseline pivots and one of two signs.  This gives \(2k-1\) states per link.  A relevance certificate chooses an unordered pair of distinct instrument values and one of two signs, giving \(2\binom{k}{2}=k(k-1)\) possibilities.  Multiplication by the design-A count gives \(M_B\).  Adding the two design-specific families gives \(M_{k,\ell}\) in (29).  Endpoint incidences not fixed by these coarse modes remain polynomial atoms inside a chart, so they do not require an additional template multiplier.

For (30), the four endpoint vectors use \(4\ell\) coordinates and the two incident coefficient vectors in each of four cells use \(8k\).  In design B, projective common-instrument and optional \(q^X\) coordinates use at most \(2k\), while margins, response masses, and four transfer scales use at most twelve more.  Hence there are at most \(N_0=4\ell+10k+12\) variables.

There are \(4k\ell\) table-factorization equations.  Endpoint simplex and support conditions contribute at most \(4\ell+4\) atoms; coefficient simplex, zero-pattern, and split-face conditions contribute at most \(24k+8\); residual definitions and transfers contribute at most \(16k+8\); and optional proportionality minors contribute at most \(4(k-1)^2\).  Shared-instrument equations, all normalizations, endpoint incidences, cycle consistency, and signed relevance contribute fewer than \(20(k\ell+k^2+\ell+1)\) further atoms.  Since \(k\ge2\) and \(\ell\ge3\), their sum is no greater than \(S_0\).

The factorization and shared-instrument equations are bilinear.  A residual \(a_{ei}(z)-\rho_z a_{ei}(z_0)\) has degree at most two; an active-link transfer equation has degree at most three; the four-link product equation has degree four; and the relevance cross-product has degree at most three after the bilinear definition of \(q^X\) is substituted.  All remaining atoms have degree no larger.  Thus \(D_0=4\).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}real\text{-}algebraic\text{-}sampling\text{-}and\text{-}existential}\) to a chart of format \((N_0,S_0,D_0)\).  The bound \(\mathsf{Samp}\) decides emptiness and, for a nonempty chart, returns a sample whose real-univariate degree and record count are bounded by \((A_S,D_S)\), proving (31).  Only one such sample is retained as \(x_0\).  Its target \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\) lies in an ordered algebraic extension of degree at most \(D_S\), because \(\tau_C\) is a linear coordinate map.

For each chart the disagreement test adds exactly the one degree-two atom in (18).  It therefore has at most \(N_0\) variables, \(S_0+1\) atoms, degree at most \(D_0=4\), and coefficient-extension degree at most \(D_S\).  The cited existential algorithm gives the first pair in (32), with \(D_E\) measured over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  Exact primitive-element conversion, square-free factorization, Thom comparison, and rational isolation give the second pair.  Across at most \(M_{k,\ell}\) charts, the product in (33) dominates the sum of all sampling, existential, and encoding records.  It also dominates \(D_S,D_E,D_R\) and their products, and hence every absolute algebraic degree created by a tower-to-primitive-element conversion.  This proves (33).

The cited singly-exponential bounds give, for a universal constant \(c\),
\[
 A_S+D_S
 \le (S_0+D_0+2)^{c(N_0+1)^c}.                            \tag{40}
\]
The same form applies to the existential stage over the algebraic coefficient extension; passing back to the original field multiplies its relative degree by at most \(D_S\).  Primitive-element and Thom normalization are singly exponential in the degrees and number of coordinates already produced.  Since \(N_0=O(Q)\), \(S_0=O(Q)\), \(D_0=4\), and \(M_{k,\ell}\le2^{Q^{c_0}}\) for a universal \(c_0\), every factor in (33) is bounded by \(2^{C_1Q^{C_1}}\).  A fixed product of such factors has the same form after increasing the universal constant, proving (34).

For arbitrary real \(\zeta\), chart coefficients belong to \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\): normalization divides only by positive \(r_e\), and every later denominator is a chart pivot whose nonzero sign is recorded.  There are finitely many charts by (29).  The cited sampling, existential, sign, primitive-element, and root routines terminate relative to the stated field and order oracles.  Thus the full real-input computation terminates.

Now suppose the reduced observable coordinates are rational and have numerator and denominator binary length at most \(L\).  Reconstructing a deleted simplex coordinate and then forming any \(r_e\) adds at most \(4k\ell\le4Q\) rational coordinates.  Taking a common denominator therefore gives numerator and denominator lengths at most \(8Q(L+1)\).  Forming \(T_e=p_e/r_e\), multiplying at most four such coefficients in a chart polynomial, and adding at most \(S_0\) monomials is bounded by \(64Q^2(L+1)=h_0\).  This proves the initial height in (35).

The integer-height part of the cited sampling theorem gives \(h_S\).  The target coordinates are rational functions of the returned primitive element with height no greater than that bound after its coordinatewise monotone normalization.  Feeding the actual coefficient-extension degree \(D_S\) and height \(h_S\) into the existential algorithm gives \(h_E\); feeding both actual degrees and heights into the primitive-element, square-free, Thom, and isolation routines gives \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\).  This proves the sequential formulas (35)--(36), and the cited normalization algorithms give the asserted square-free integer and rational-isolating representations.

The cited height bounds have the form
\[
 h_{\mathrm{out}}
 \le (h_{\mathrm{in}}+1)^{2^{C_2Q^{C_2}}}                 \tag{41}
\]
at each of the fixed number of stages, after (40) and the extension degrees are substituted.  Composing a fixed number of powers in (41) multiplies their exponents, which remains at most \(2^{C_3Q^{C_3}}\).  Since \(h_0\le2^{C_3Q^{C_3}}(L+1)\), increasing the universal constant yields (37).  Thus every loop and every rational-input algebraic operation has an explicit finite bound.  The executed sequence is chart sampling followed by chartwise existential disagreement sampling; component and projection routines play no role in either the decision or these bounds.
